Action.description:
What changed — and for `requested`, what did not: the person was **asked** and has not
agreed. Stored as text under a `check` constraint, as `lists::MembershipStatus` is.

ApiKeySummary.description: A key as listed: its prefix identifies it, nothing in it can authenticate.

note.description: States, so no client has to guess, that deleting did not delete data.

AuditEntry.description:
One audit row, as stored. `metadata` is returned verbatim, which is why writers must never put
a secret in it.

`actor_email` and `actor_api_key_prefix` name the actor the ids point at, resolved by the two
LEFT JOINs in `list`. They are a convenience for display, not a second identity: the ids stay
authoritative, and either name is `None` once the user or key behind it has been deleted —
`audit_log` has no foreign keys on purpose, so its rows outlive both.

actor_api_key_prefix.description: The key's public prefix, without the `nm_` scheme: a key is shown as `nm_{prefix}`.

children.description:
`no_recursion` because `Block` contains itself here. Without it `utoipa` inlines the
nested schema for ever and the document build overflows its stack; with it the field
is a `$ref` to this same component, which is what the generated TypeScript needs to
describe a column holding blocks.

Block.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` on both enums: this is JSON from anything holding a session, and a field
a variant does not define is refused rather than quietly dropped. The editor rejects the same
shapes, but that is a convenience for the operator, not a boundary.

BlockLevel.description: Whose block it is: this workspace's own, or one set instance-wide that every workspace inherits.

BrandKit.description:
The kit as the API shows it and as the row stores it.

`palette` and `footer` are passed through **whole**. Contract section 8: a kit written by a
newer version must survive a round trip through an older screen rather than being silently
stripped, so the known keys are validated and every other key is kept exactly as it arrived.

footer.description:
`{ "text", "address" }`. `address` is the CAN-SPAM / CASL postal address. An open map, for
the same reason as `palette`.

logo_url.description:
`http` or `https` only (contract section 11): `mailto:` and `tel:` are meaningless as an
image source, so the logo takes a narrower set than the link allowlist.

palette.description:
`{ "background", "text", "accent", "accent_text" }`, each `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`. Other keys
are kept untouched, which is why the schema is an open map and not a closed object: a
client has to be able to send back a key its own version does not know.

BulkResult.description:
What a bulk action did, as two numbers taken from the same statement. `affected` is how many
contacts it changed; `selected` is how much of the frozen set the action still found, less the
exclusions. `affected` is lower whenever some were already in the wanted state, so the UI can
say "N of M".

issued.description:
How many the selection stood for when it was made. `selected` below it means contacts in
the frozen set were deleted between the selection and the action, or were excluded; it can
never be above it, because the set was written down and nothing re-evaluates a predicate.

oneOf.description:
Only for `subscribe`: the status the new memberships were written with. `pending` means
the contacts are on a double-opt-in list and not mailable until they confirm, and NM has
no confirmation flow yet: `affected` is not a count of people who can be mailed.

BulkTarget.description:
What a bulk route acts on: exactly one of a filter selection or an explicit list of contacts.

The three bulk bodies spell their fields out and deny unknown ones, on purpose: `excluded_ids`
defaults to empty, so a misspelt `excluded_id` that was quietly ignored would run the action
on exactly the contacts the user meant to spare. `serde(flatten)` cannot be combined with
`deny_unknown_fields`, so do not factor these back into one flattened struct, and give any
new optional field here a reason to exist.

confirmed_count.description:
How many contacts the confirmation showed: the size of the frozen set **less**
`excluded_ids` — the number on the button, not the number the token was issued for.
Required with `selection_token`, refused with `ids`.

The action is refused `409` if it would reach **more** contacts than this. Reaching fewer
is not refused: a contact deleted between the selection and the action is simply absent,
and the gap between `selected` and `affected` reports it. Sending the pre-exclusion size
instead would send a number the server already holds signed into the token, which can
never be below what the action reaches and so can never refuse anything.

excluded_ids.description: Contacts to leave out of a `selection_token`. At most 10 000.

ids.description:
These contacts and no others, e.g. the ticked rows of a table: at most 10 000. Ids that are
not in this workspace select nothing. Cannot be combined with `excluded_ids`.

selection_token.description:
From `POST /contacts/selection`: the contacts it froze, less `excluded_ids`. Send this or
`ids`, not both and not neither.

CampaignCounts.description: Contract section 2. `queued` is what is left: in flight included.

CampaignEstimate.description: How many contacts the audience is, or that there are too many to count in two seconds.

CampaignPreview.description: One variant as one sample recipient would receive it, footer included.

CampaignSchedule.description: The schedule as typed, and the instant the server resolved it to.

local.description: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, no zone; null means send now.

send_at.description: RFC 5545 resolution of `local` in `zone`; for `recipient_local`, the earliest zone's.

CampaignState.description: Where a campaign is in the machine of spec §4.1. Stored as text under a `check` constraint.

CampaignVariant.description: One content variant. A single variant is an ordinary send.

from_name.description: Overrides the campaign's `from_name` for this variant.

subject.description: Merge-tag grammar, as plain text; compiled at save and at freeze.

ab_test_percent.description: 10..100, only with two or more variants; 100 is a pure split with no winner phase.

awaiting_winner.description: The A/B test is over and the remainder waits for `…/winner`.

variants.description: 1..4 once saved with content; empty on a fresh draft.

winner.description: The variant index an admin picked.

challenge_id.description: Send back with the browser's answer.

options.description: The WebAuthn `publicKey` options object, as `@simplewebauthn/browser` expects.

Check.description: Which checker produced the finding. Contract section 12: `"lint" | "link"`.

CheckResult.description:
One check's verdict. On the wire (and in `sending_domains.checks`) it is
`{"status": "pass"}`, `{"status": "fail", "reason": "..."}` or `{"status": "not_checked"}`.

A `Fail` reason is shown to an operator and stored, so it must never carry key material: a
mismatched DKIM `p=` says that it differs and names neither value.

oneOf.description: The column is not imported. Also what a proposal says when it is unsure.
A custom field, by its key.

value.description: A custom field, by its key.

ColumnTarget.description: What one CSV column is written to.

ConsentEntry.description:
One row of the log, with the list's name joined on.

**The evidence columns are the point of the row**, not decoration on it: a row that says
`subscribed` without saying how is what this milestone exists to prevent. `ip` and
`user_agent` are the subscriber's own, written only by the public routes where the request
really was theirs; an operator or API change carries neither and names the actor in
`source_ref` instead.

action.description:
`requested` means the person was **asked** and has not agreed — a double opt-in that is
still pending. It is not a softer `subscribed`.

ip.description: The subscriber's own address, on the public routes only.

list_id.description:
Null for a workspace-wide change, and for a row whose list has since been deleted —
`0020_consent_log.sql` nulls the pointer and keeps the evidence.

list_name.description: The list's name now. Null whenever `list_id` is.

source.description:
The code path the change arrived by, never who made it: a session-authenticated operator
using bulk subscribe is recorded as `api`.

source_ref.description: Whatever caused the change: the form id, the import id, the user or API key id.

token_jti.description: The nonce of the public token that authorised the change: *which* link was clicked.

user_agent.description: The subscriber's own, on the public routes only.

attributes.description: Custom field values by field key. Values of archived fields stay readable here.

ContactField.description:
A built-in contact column an import may write: the exporter's own header for it. `id`,
`created_at`, `updated_at` and `suppressed` are not here on purpose: the first three are the
database's, and an import may not bypass or lift a suppression (spec 7.5).

ContactList.description: One list a contact is on, as the contact's page shows it.

ContactSort.description:
What a contact list is ordered by. Only keys with an index (`contacts_keyset_created`,
`contacts_keyset_email`) are offered: a sort by name would sort the whole workspace per page.

CountState.description:
Why a row has the number it has, or has none.

One value per fact, so a null `count` never has to be guessed at: `exact` and `estimated`
carry a number, and `no_estimate`, `unreadable` and `failed` each carry none for a different
reason, spelled out below.

CreatedApiKey.description: The one response that carries the key.

CreatedInvite.description: The one response that carries the token, inside `invite_url`.

Dedup.description: What to do with a row whose address is already a contact in the workspace (spec 7.3).

archived_at.description: Set when the field was deleted. Contacts keep their values until the field is purged.

options.description: The allowed values of a `select` or `multi_select` field; empty for every other kind.

DnsChecks.description:
The four checks. Every field defaults to `NotChecked`, so the `{}` a new domain starts with
and a document written before a check existed both read back as "not run".

Doc.description:
The block tree as it crosses the wire and as `templates.tree` stores it: an object, because the
column's `templates_tree_is_object` check refuses a bare array.

Eligibility.description: Whether a contact may be mailed, and if a standing block stops it, which one.

oneOf.description:
The block that stops this address, whether it is this workspace's or the whole instance's.
It says nothing about any other address. A list membership that is `pending` or
`unsubscribed` is a separate reason a contact is not mailed on that list, and is not here.

FieldKind.description: How a field's value is typed, stored as snake_case text (a `check` constraint, not an enum).

Finding.description:
Contract section 12. `at` is a PATH into the block tree, not an index: `Columns.children` is an
array of arrays, so `[3, 1, 0]` is the first block of the second column of block 3. `None`
means the finding is about the whole email.

credential.description: The browser's `PublicKeyCredential`, in WebAuthn JSON form.

list_ids.description:
The lists one submission subscribes to, ascending. The Rust-side projection of the
`form_lists` rows, so it is a set: the order a client sent is not kept.

name.description: The operator's own name for it; never shown to a submitter.

redirect_url.description:
Where a successful submission is to be sent. Absolute `http`/`https` only; see
[`validate_redirect_url`].

slug.description: Unique in the workspace. It is what names the form in its public URL.

label.description: What the page prints beside the input.

oneOf.description:
A custom field, by its `custom_fields.key`. Checked against the workspace's live
definitions at write time: a form collecting into a field that is not there collects into
nowhere, and the operator would find out only once the submissions had happened.

value.description:
A custom field, by its `custom_fields.key`. Checked against the workspace's live
definitions at write time: a form collecting into a field that is not there collects into
nowhere, and the operator would find out only once the submissions had happened.

FormTarget.description:
What one field of a form collects.

This is deliberately **not** `contacts::import::ContactField`, which the CSV importer uses.
That enum carries `Lists`, and a public form field targeting it would let whoever fills the
form in name the lists they join — the form's lists are the operator's decision, not the
submitter's. It also has no custom-field case, which spec §7.3 requires.

There is therefore no `Lists` variant here and there must never be one. Serde refuses an
unknown tag, so a hand-written body naming `"lists"` fails to deserialise and the request is
refused before any handler sees it; `tests/forms.rs` pins that through the API, because no
Rust-level test can exercise a variant that does not exist.

ImportErrorRow.description:
One rejected row, as the operator has to read it: which row, which column, why, and the cell
that did it.

column_name.description: The column to blame, where one column is to blame.

row_number.description:
**The line the row is on in the file, as a spreadsheet numbers them**, which is what an
operator has to open the file at. The header row takes line 1 of a headed file and a blank
line takes a number of its own, so the first data row of a headed file is line 2 and the
second is line 3.

It is therefore **not** an index into the data rows and does not run alongside
`total_rows`, which counts data rows only: a headed file of 10 rows reports
`total_rows = 10` and may hold an error on line 11.

value.description:
The offending cell as the file held it, cut short. Nothing else of the file is echoed, and
a row refused because its address was **erased on request** carries no value at all: the
erasure took that address out of the database, and this list is served for as long as the
import exists. `row_number` says which line of the file to look at.

ImportReport.description:
What an import did, count by count (spec 7.5): *"'Imported 940,000 of 1,000,000' with no
breakdown is not a report."*

**`imported`, `updated`, `skipped`, `collapsed` and `failed` are the five row-level counts**,
and they are mutually exclusive: every row of the file lands in exactly one of them, so on a
`complete` import they sum to `total_rows`. (A `failed` import died part-way: its counts are
what it got to, and `total_rows` may still be `null`.)

**`suppressed` and `memberships_declined` are not row-level.** They describe rows already
counted among the five — a suppressed address is still an imported or updated contact, and a
declined subscription belongs to one — so adding all seven counts those rows twice.

collapsed.description:
Rows a later row of the same file names the same address as. Not `skipped`: the file
de-duplicated itself, and the database never had these rows.

error_reason.description:
Why the import as a whole failed, and `null` otherwise. Never one row's reason: those are
in `GET /imports/{id}/errors`.

errors_recorded.description:
How many rejected rows `GET /imports/{id}/errors` can show. An import keeps at most
[`MAX_IMPORT_ERRORS`](super::staging::MAX_IMPORT_ERRORS) of them while `failed` counts
every one, so **when this is less than `failed`, that list is the first `errors_recorded`
rejected rows in file order and not all of them** — an operator who pages to the end of it
has not seen everything wrong with the file, and has to be told so.

failed.description: Every rejected row. [`ImportReport::errors_recorded`] is how many of them were kept.

filename.description: What the file was called when it was uploaded. A label; nothing opens it.

imported.description: Rows that became a new contact.

memberships_declined.description:
Subscriptions this import asked for and did not get, because the address is already
`unsubscribed` on that list. The contact itself was still imported or updated.

skipped.description: Rows left alone because the contact already existed (`skip existing`).

status.description:
`pending`, `complete` or `failed`.

**`running` is a state the database allows and this server never serves.** The run is one
transaction inside `POST /imports/{id}/start`, which writes `running` and commits once at
the end, so no reader outside that transaction ever sees it. A row can only be left
`running` by a process that died mid-run, and the next boot sweeps those to `failed`
before anything is served. Do not write a client that waits for it. When the run moves off
the request it will become reachable, and that is the change that should make this a typed
enum.

suppressed.description:
Imported or updated contacts whose address or domain is suppressed. They exist and they
are not mailable — said here rather than discovered at send time.

total_rows.description:
`null` while the `COPY` is still counting the file. Not `0`, which would report an empty
file for an import that has not read its first row.

updated.description: Rows applied to a contact that already existed.

InvitePreview.description: What the invitee sees before accepting.

account_exists.description: Whether to show a sign-in or a set-a-password form.

InviteSummary.description: An open invite as the workspace's admins see it: no token, no URL.

Kind.description: How a template is authored. The database stores it as text under a `check` constraint.

double_optin.description:
`true`: a new member is `pending` until they confirm. `false`: a new member is
`subscribed` at once.

visibility.description:
Whether the preference center offers this list to somebody who is not on it. A `private`
list is still shown there to its own members, so hiding one never leaves a subscriber
unable to leave it (`public::unsubscribe::topics`).

ListMember.description: A contact's standing on one list.

subscribed_at.description: Null while `pending`, and after an unsubscribe is undone on a double-opt-in list.

unsubscribed_at.description: Set only while the status is `unsubscribed`.

methods.description: The second factors on offer; present only for `mfa_required`.

status.description:
`ok` once signed in; `mfa_required` when a second factor must follow at
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/totp` (the cookie set is then a 10-minute pending session).

MembershipStatus.description:
What a membership row says. It means the same on every list: `Pending` is written only on a
double-opt-in list, `Subscribed` is written at once on a single-opt-in one, and nothing here
depends on the list's setting. A `Pending` row can outlive the list's
double opt-in being switched off: it still means "not confirmed" and is not mailable.

role.description: `viewer`, `editor` or `admin`, and no higher than the caller's own role.

NewCampaign.description: A campaign to create. Everything but `name` may be filled in later.

NewContact.description: A contact to insert. Nothing here is trusted: `create` validates every field.

attributes.description: Custom field values by field key; see `validate_attributes` for what each kind accepts.

email.description: Normalised (trimmed, NFC, lowercased) before it is stored.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as `Europe/London`.

key.description:
`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`. The JSONB key every contact's value is stored under; it cannot
change afterwards.

options.description: Required (1-200 distinct values) for `select` and `multi_select`; omit for every other kind.

fields.description: The page's inputs. Exactly one must target `email`.

list_ids.description: At least one, at most 25. Each must be a list of this workspace.

redirect_url.description: Absolute `http`/`https` only. Absent or `null` means the form has no redirect.

slug.description: Unique in the workspace. It is what names the form in its public URL.

NewImport.description: The request body, for the document: the one part, named `file`.

file.description: The CSV file. Its name is kept as a label and is never used as a path.

max_connections.description:
How many connections to this relay one sender process keeps parked for reuse.
Default 4. **Not a cap on concurrent connections** — a send that finds none parked
opens a new one. `rate_limit_per_minute` is what holds a relay to what it will take.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: What the relay's operator says it allows. At least 1.

NewSelection.description:
The body of `POST /contacts/selection`: which contacts to freeze.

The grid's filter fields, spelled out rather than nested, for the reason `BulkTarget` gives:
unknown fields are refused, and a misspelt `tag_id_` that was quietly ignored here would
freeze every contact in the workspace.

list_id.description: Contacts with a membership row on this list, whatever its status.

oneOf.description: Narrows `list_id` to the memberships with this status; refused without a `list_id`.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring of the address or name; at least 3 characters.

segment_id.description:
A saved segment, whose stored rules narrow the selection further. An id that is not a
segment of this workspace is a `404`, never read as "no rules".

dkim_private_key.description:
An unencrypted RSA private key in PEM (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` or `BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`).
Required when `signing` is `app`. Stored encrypted and never returned.

dkim_selector.description: Where the DKIM key is published, as `{selector}._domainkey.{domain}`. Default `nm1`.

domain.description:
The domain mail is sent from, as in `news@example.com`'s `example.com`. ASCII (punycode for
an internationalized name); stored lower case.

from_name.description: Display name a campaign from this domain defaults to.

return_path_domain.description: A domain whose CNAME carries bounces to the relay. The sending domain or a subdomain of it.

signing.description: `relay` if the relay signs, `app` if this product does.

NewSuppression.description:
A suppression to add. `scope` decides which of `email` and `domain` is required, and the other
must be absent.

domain.description: Required for `domain`, such as `spam.example`. Matches that exact domain only: subdomains are NOT covered (`spam.example` leaves `mail.spam.example` mailable).

email.description: Required for `address`. Normalised (trimmed, NFC, lowercased) before it is stored.

note.description: Up to 500 characters; line breaks are allowed.

reason.description: Anything but `gdpr_erasure`, which only erasing a contact writes.

source.description: Required when `kind` is `mjml` or `html`, and refused otherwise. May not be empty.

oneOf.description: Required when `kind` is `blocks`, and refused otherwise.

timezone.description: An IANA zone such as `Europe/London`; defaults to `UTC`.

items.description: A key as listed: its prefix identifies it, nothing in it can authenticate.

One audit row, as stored. `metadata` is returned verbatim, which is why writers must never put
a secret in it.

`actor_email` and `actor_api_key_prefix` name the actor the ids point at, resolved by the two
LEFT JOINs in `list`. They are a convenience for display, not a second identity: the ids stay
authoritative, and either name is `None` once the user or key behind it has been deleted —
`audit_log` has no foreign keys on purpose, so its rows outlive both.

actor_api_key_prefix.description: The key's public prefix, without the `nm_` scheme: a key is shown as `nm_{prefix}`.

items.description:
One row of the log, with the list's name joined on.

**The evidence columns are the point of the row**, not decoration on it: a row that says
`subscribed` without saying how is what this milestone exists to prevent. `ip` and
`user_agent` are the subscriber's own, written only by the public routes where the request
really was theirs; an operator or API change carries neither and names the actor in
`source_ref` instead.

action.description:
`requested` means the person was **asked** and has not agreed — a double opt-in that is
still pending. It is not a softer `subscribed`.

ip.description: The subscriber's own address, on the public routes only.

list_id.description:
Null for a workspace-wide change, and for a row whose list has since been deleted —
`0020_consent_log.sql` nulls the pointer and keeps the evidence.

list_name.description: The list's name now. Null whenever `list_id` is.

source.description:
The code path the change arrived by, never who made it: a session-authenticated operator
using bulk subscribe is recorded as `api`.

source_ref.description: Whatever caused the change: the form id, the import id, the user or API key id.

token_jti.description: The nonce of the public token that authorised the change: *which* link was clicked.

user_agent.description: The subscriber's own, on the public routes only.

attributes.description: Custom field values by field key. Values of archived fields stay readable here.

items.description: One list a contact is on, as the contact's page shows it.

archived_at.description: Set when the field was deleted. Contacts keep their values until the field is purged.

options.description: The allowed values of a `select` or `multi_select` field; empty for every other kind.

list_ids.description:
The lists one submission subscribes to, ascending. The Rust-side projection of the
`form_lists` rows, so it is a set: the order a client sent is not kept.

name.description: The operator's own name for it; never shown to a submitter.

redirect_url.description:
Where a successful submission is to be sent. Absolute `http`/`https` only; see
[`validate_redirect_url`].

slug.description: Unique in the workspace. It is what names the form in its public URL.

items.description:
One rejected row, as the operator has to read it: which row, which column, why, and the cell
that did it.

column_name.description: The column to blame, where one column is to blame.

row_number.description:
**The line the row is on in the file, as a spreadsheet numbers them**, which is what an
operator has to open the file at. The header row takes line 1 of a headed file and a blank
line takes a number of its own, so the first data row of a headed file is line 2 and the
second is line 3.

It is therefore **not** an index into the data rows and does not run alongside
`total_rows`, which counts data rows only: a headed file of 10 rows reports
`total_rows = 10` and may hold an error on line 11.

value.description:
The offending cell as the file held it, cut short. Nothing else of the file is echoed, and
a row refused because its address was **erased on request** carries no value at all: the
erasure took that address out of the database, and this list is served for as long as the
import exists. `row_number` says which line of the file to look at.

items.description:
What an import did, count by count (spec 7.5): *"'Imported 940,000 of 1,000,000' with no
breakdown is not a report."*

**`imported`, `updated`, `skipped`, `collapsed` and `failed` are the five row-level counts**,
and they are mutually exclusive: every row of the file lands in exactly one of them, so on a
`complete` import they sum to `total_rows`. (A `failed` import died part-way: its counts are
what it got to, and `total_rows` may still be `null`.)

**`suppressed` and `memberships_declined` are not row-level.** They describe rows already
counted among the five — a suppressed address is still an imported or updated contact, and a
declined subscription belongs to one — so adding all seven counts those rows twice.

collapsed.description:
Rows a later row of the same file names the same address as. Not `skipped`: the file
de-duplicated itself, and the database never had these rows.

error_reason.description:
Why the import as a whole failed, and `null` otherwise. Never one row's reason: those are
in `GET /imports/{id}/errors`.

errors_recorded.description:
How many rejected rows `GET /imports/{id}/errors` can show. An import keeps at most
[`MAX_IMPORT_ERRORS`](super::staging::MAX_IMPORT_ERRORS) of them while `failed` counts
every one, so **when this is less than `failed`, that list is the first `errors_recorded`
rejected rows in file order and not all of them** — an operator who pages to the end of it
has not seen everything wrong with the file, and has to be told so.

failed.description: Every rejected row. [`ImportReport::errors_recorded`] is how many of them were kept.

filename.description: What the file was called when it was uploaded. A label; nothing opens it.

imported.description: Rows that became a new contact.

memberships_declined.description:
Subscriptions this import asked for and did not get, because the address is already
`unsubscribed` on that list. The contact itself was still imported or updated.

skipped.description: Rows left alone because the contact already existed (`skip existing`).

status.description:
`pending`, `complete` or `failed`.

**`running` is a state the database allows and this server never serves.** The run is one
transaction inside `POST /imports/{id}/start`, which writes `running` and commits once at
the end, so no reader outside that transaction ever sees it. A row can only be left
`running` by a process that died mid-run, and the next boot sweeps those to `failed`
before anything is served. Do not write a client that waits for it. When the run moves off
the request it will become reachable, and that is the change that should make this a typed
enum.

suppressed.description:
Imported or updated contacts whose address or domain is suppressed. They exist and they
are not mailable — said here rather than discovered at send time.

total_rows.description:
`null` while the `COPY` is still counting the file. Not `0`, which would report an empty
file for an import that has not read its first row.

updated.description: Rows applied to a contact that already existed.

items.description: An open invite as the workspace's admins see it: no token, no URL.

double_optin.description:
`true`: a new member is `pending` until they confirm. `false`: a new member is
`subscribed` at once.

visibility.description:
Whether the preference center offers this list to somebody who is not on it. A `private`
list is still shown there to its own members, so hiding one never leaves a subscriber
unable to leave it (`public::unsubscribe::topics`).

items.description: A contact's standing on one list.

subscribed_at.description: Null while `pending`, and after an unsubscribe is undone on a double-opt-in list.

unsubscribed_at.description: Set only while the status is `unsubscribed`.

items.description: A passkey as listed: nothing in it can authenticate.

A relay as the API shows it. There is no password field, on purpose: `has_password` is all an
operator may learn about it.

has_password.description: Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

rules.description: The rule document, `{match, rules}`. Replaced as a whole on every edit.

version.description: Starts at 1 and moves only when an edit changes `rules`: a rename leaves it alone.

items.description:
A sending domain as the API shows it. There is no private-key field, on purpose: `has_dkim_key`
says one is stored, and `dkim_public_txt` is the public half, derived here from the stored key.

checked_at.description: When `checks` was written; null if the checker has never run for this configuration.

checks.description: The DNS checker's last result; every check is `not_checked` until it has run.

dkim_public_txt.description:
What to publish as a TXT record at `{dkim_selector}._domainkey.{domain}`: `v=DKIM1; k=rsa;
p=...`, the public half of the stored key. Null when no key is stored. Derived on the
server when the key is saved and stored beside it, never from anything but that key, so
reading it does not decrypt the key; the private key is never returned.

domain.description: Lower case. Unique in the workspace, and fixed once created.

from_name.description: The display name a campaign from this domain defaults to.

has_dkim_key.description: Whether a DKIM private key is stored. The key itself is never returned.

items.description: A suppression as the API shows it. There is deliberately no hash field here.

email.description: Address scope only; null on an erasure tombstone, whose plaintext was destroyed.

lifted_at.description: Set when lifted. A lifted row stays, as history.

workspace_id.description: Null for an instance-wide suppression, which applies to every workspace.

items.description: What the list shows and the campaign picker reads (issue 50 item 1): no `tree`, no `source`.
A workspace as one caller sees it: `role` is the caller's own.

PasskeySummary.description: A passkey as listed: nothing in it can authenticate.

Preview.description: How many contacts a rule document matches.

count.description:
The matching contacts, or `null` when no honest number can be given — the document filters
on a custom attribute, which carries no statistics for the planner to estimate from. The
rule builder shows "too many to count exactly" for `null`.

exact.description: `false` when `count` is the planner's estimate, or when there is no count at all.

PreviewRequest.description: The body of `POST /segments/preview`: a rule document that need not be saved, or savable.

PreviewResult.description:
Contract section 12, exactly. `html` is a whole document; a failed render or a failed check is
an ERROR and never an `Ok` with an empty `findings`, which the preview panel reads as a pass.

affected.description: Contacts whose value for the field was removed.

Reason.description: Why an address is blocked. Stored as text under a `check` constraint, not a Postgres enum.

RelayView.description:
A relay as the API shows it. There is no password field, on purpose: `has_password` is all an
operator may learn about it.

has_password.description: Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

Role.description:
A member's role, stored as lowercase text. Variants run from least to most privileged:
`authorize` compares roles with `<`, so the order here is load-bearing.

Rule.description:
The stable machine-readable name of a rule. A help link or a suppression hangs off this; the
human message is not that.

oneOf.description: The tag as the operator typed it, braces included. The compiled AST never crosses the wire.

ScheduleMode.description:
How `schedule_local` is read: one instant for everyone, or that wall-clock time in each
recipient's own zone (spec §4.3).

Security.description: How the connection to the relay is secured. Stored as text under a `check` constraint.

rules.description: The rule document, `{match, rules}`. Replaced as a whole on every edit.

version.description: Starts at 1 and moves only when an edit changes `rules`: a rename leaves it alone.

SegmentCount.description:
One segment's count in a batch. `Preview`'s `took_ms` has no meaning per row: the batch is one
statement and every row in it took the same time.

count.description:
The number, for `exact` and `estimated`. Null for `no_estimate`, `unreadable` and
`failed`, which is what `state` is there to tell apart.

SelectionToken.description: A materialised selection: the snapshot that was written, and the token for it.

selected.description:
How many contacts were frozen. Exact for free — it is the materialising insert's own
`rows_affected` — and deliberately exempt from the 150 ms p95 target, like
`GET /lists/{id}/mailable-count`: materialising a million ids is measured at 4,887 ms. The
UI shows a skeleton until it lands. It is never kept as a counter on a table:
hand-maintained counters drift.

selection_token.description:
Valid for one hour. Pass it to a `bulk/*` route, with `confirmed_count`.

It names `snapshot_id` and carries no predicate, so it is issued for every selection,
`segment_id` included: there is no longer any predicate in it that could describe a wider
set than the one that was frozen.

snapshot_id.description:
The frozen set, by id: exactly the contacts that matched, written down. It expires in an
hour, and a new selection by the same person in this workspace supersedes it.

SendingDomainView.description:
A sending domain as the API shows it. There is no private-key field, on purpose: `has_dkim_key`
says one is stored, and `dkim_public_txt` is the public half, derived here from the stored key.

checked_at.description: When `checks` was written; null if the checker has never run for this configuration.

checks.description: The DNS checker's last result; every check is `not_checked` until it has run.

dkim_public_txt.description:
What to publish as a TXT record at `{dkim_selector}._domainkey.{domain}`: `v=DKIM1; k=rsa;
p=...`, the public half of the stored key. Null when no key is stored. Derived on the
server when the key is saved and stored beside it, never from anything but that key, so
reading it does not decrypt the key; the private key is never returned.

domain.description: Lower case. Unique in the workspace, and fixed once created.

from_name.description: The display name a campaign from this domain defaults to.

has_dkim_key.description: Whether a DKIM private key is stored. The key itself is never returned.

Severity.description:
Contract section 12: `error` means the sent email will be wrong or unsafe for a recipient,
`warning` means probably a mistake but an operator may mean it.

Signing.description: Who signs the domain's mail with DKIM. Stored as text under a `check` constraint.

Source.description:
What caused the change. **The code path, never the actor**: a session-authenticated operator
using bulk subscribe is `Api`, because that is the writer the change went through.

StartImport.description: The confirmed mapping, and the run.

dedup.description:
What to do with a row whose address is already a contact here. `update_existing` by
default, which is spec 7.3's blank-cell rule: a blank leaves the stored value alone.

delimiter.description:
Replaces the delimiter the upload sniffed: one of `,`, `;`, a tab or `|`. Left out, the
stored one is used — the file is never sniffed a second time.

has_header.description: Replaces the header guess the upload made. Left out, the stored one is used.

list_id.description:
A list in this workspace to subscribe every imported contact to. The file's own `lists`
column, where it has one, is added to this rather than replacing it.

mapping.description:
One target per CSV column, in the file's column order. One column must be `email`, and no
two columns may name the same single-write target.

Suppression.description: A suppression as the API shows it. There is deliberately no hash field here.

email.description: Address scope only; null on an erasure tombstone, whose plaintext was destroyed.

lifted_at.description: Set when lifted. A lifted row stays, as history.

workspace_id.description: Null for an instance-wide suppression, which applies to every workspace.

SuppressionBlock.description:
The standing block that stops one address being mailed, and nothing else about it: not the
row's id, note or who made it, and never another address.

Named for what it blocks rather than `Block`, because `components.schemas` is ONE flat map
keyed by the type's name and `template::block::Block` is a different thing entirely. Two types
sharing a key do not collide loudly: the second insert replaces the first and every `$ref`
still resolves, so one of them ships with the other's shape (`schema_names_are_unique`).

scope.description: Whether it blocks this one address or every address on its domain.

TemplatePreviewRequest.description:
What to preview. Send the document being edited to preview unsaved changes; send neither key
to preview what is stored.

TemplateSummary.description: What the list shows and the campaign picker reads (issue 50 item 1): no `tree`, no `source`.

TemplateView.description:
A template as the API shows it. `compiled` is never returned: it is the renderer's own
storage, it is derived from the two columns below, and the editor has no use for an AST
(contract section 4).

source.description: The MJML or HTML the operator wrote; null for a `blocks` template.

oneOf.description: The block document, for a `blocks` template; null for a raw one.

UpdateCampaign.description: A key left out is left alone; `null` clears a nullable one.

UpdateContact.description:
A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) of a contact: a field left out is left alone, and an explicit
`null` removes it. The address cannot change, so `email` is an unknown field here and is
rejected, not ignored.

attributes.description:
Merged into the stored attributes key by key: a key left out keeps its value. A key set to
`null` is removed, also for an archived field; any other value for an archived field is
refused. `attributes` itself cannot be `null`.

first_name.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

last_name.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as `Europe/London`. `null` clears it.

UpdateCustomField.description:
`key` is immutable, so an unknown field (`key` included) is rejected, not ignored. `kind` is
accepted only so that a change can be refused with a message that says why.

oneOf.description: Must equal the field's current kind: changing it is not supported yet.

fields.description: Replaces the fields outright. Cannot be `null`.

list_ids.description: Replaces the lists outright. Cannot be `null` or empty.

redirect_url.description: `null` clears it, leaving the form with no redirect.

UpdateList.description:
A field left out is left alone. `null` clears `description` to an empty string; on any other
field it is `422`, because there is nothing to clear it to and ignoring it would look like
success.

description.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

double_optin.description:
Only decides the status of members added from now on. A member already `pending` stays
`pending` (not mailable) when this is switched off. Cannot be `null`.

UpdateRelay.description:
A field left out is left alone. `username` and `password` may be `null`, which clears them; on
any other field `null` is `422`, because there is nothing to clear it to.

password.description: Absent keeps the stored password; `null` removes it; a string replaces it.

UpdateSegment.description:
A merge patch (RFC 7386) of everything but `rules`: a field left out is left alone, `null`
clears `description`. `rules` is the exception: it is **replaced as a whole**, never merged
into the stored document. A patch carrying `rules` must carry the entire document; a partial
one is `422`, because merging `{"match": "any"}` into the old document would flip the
connective and silently keep the old rules.

description.description: `null` clears it to an empty string.

name.description: Cannot be `null`: leave it out to leave it alone.

rules.description:
The whole replacement document. Cannot be `null` (refused, not ignored): leave it out to
leave the rules alone. Resending the stored document is accepted unchanged, even if it
names a field that has since been archived.

UpdateSendingDomain.description:
A field left out is left alone. `from_name`, `return_path_domain` and `dkim_private_key` may be
`null`, which clears them; on any other field `null` is `422`, because there is nothing to
clear it to. The domain itself cannot be changed: delete the domain and add the new one.

Changing `signing`, `dkim_selector`, `return_path_domain` or `dkim_private_key` resets `checks`
and the acknowledgement, which no longer describe what is configured.

dkim_private_key.description: Absent keeps the stored key; `null` removes it; a PEM string replaces it.

send_unverified_acknowledged.description:
`true` records that an admin accepts sending from this domain while its checks are not all
passing, and stamps the time; `false` withdraws it. Editing `signing`, `dkim_selector`,
`return_path_domain` or `dkim_private_key` withdraws it too, unless this is sent in the same
request, in which case it is the acknowledgement of the configuration being saved.

UpdateTemplate.description:
A field left out is left alone. `kind` is not patchable: it decides which column holds the
document, so changing it is a different template, not an edit to this one.

UpdateWorkspace.description: The slug cannot change in M0, so an unknown field (`slug` included) is rejected, not ignored.

has_header.description: A guess: the first row is a header unless it holds an email address.

name.description: The header cell, or `Column N` when the file has no header row.

proposed.description:
`ignore` when the server is not sure: a blank costs one dropdown, a wrong guess writes the
wrong column into the wrong field.

samples.description: Up to five non-blank values from the first 100 rows, as a spreadsheet shows them.

Visibility.description: Stored as text under a `check` constraint, not a Postgres enum.

Workspace.description: A workspace as one caller sees it: `role` is the caller's own.
